absent: Hash allocation and slot query helpers beyond prctl dispatch and custom flag semantics.
Complete waiter hash computation with bucket selection and private table lookup when enabled.
Remainder of owner fixup logic after truncation with related unlock and requeue PI flows.
Task exit cleanup for PI state with robust list handling and full futex state lifecycle.
Underlying real-time mutex blocking with owner tracking and wake-queue mechanics.
Classic and second-generation system-call entries with timeout and bitset handling beyond flag conversion.
Per-node allocation helpers with large-order fallback details and runtime constant publication.

findings.text: The hash control handler dispatches on an operation selector where PR_FUTEX_HASH_SET_SLOTS requests resizing with a caller supplied slot count and rejects any non-zero spare argument with EINVAL and PR_FUTEX_HASH_GET_SLOTS requests the current slot count and unrecognized selectors yield EINVAL.

Boot initialization sizes the global hash from topology with a fixed small size for tiny builds and otherwise scaling by possible processor count divided by possible node count with a lower bound and rounding up to a power of two. Final mask in __futex_mask with shift in __futex_shift derives from the chosen size and per-node tables published for lookup use a large-order fallback with every bucket initialized before geometry reporting.
The internal futex header is protected against multiple inclusion by a conventional guard macro.

Internal size selection occupies two low bits where FLAGS_SIZE_8 corresponds to value 0x0000 and FLAGS_SIZE_16 to 0x0001 and FLAGS_SIZE_32 to 0x0002 and FLAGS_SIZE_64 to 0x0003 while the mask FLAGS_SIZE_MASK isolating the selector is 0x0003.

The shared marker FLAGS_SHARED has build-dependent encodings where one configuration defines it as 0x0010 and the alternate defines it as 0x0000 reflecting whether shared versus private distinction is tracked in flags.

Additional internal flag bits use distinct powers of two where FLAGS_CLOCKRT corresponds to 0x0020 and FLAGS_HAS_TIMEOUT to 0x0040 and FLAGS_NUMA to 0x0080 and FLAGS_STRICT to 0x0100 and FLAGS_MPOL to 0x0200 and FLAGS_ROBUST_UNLOCK to 0x0400 and FLAGS_ROBUST_LIST32 to 0x0800.

The mask of accepted second-generation option bits FUTEX2_VALID_MASK combines the size selector mask FUTEX2_SIZE_MASK with the NUMA bit FUTEX2_NUMA and the memory-policy bit FUTEX2_MPOL and the private bit FUTEX2_PRIVATE.

Conversion from classic operation encoding to internal flags defaults to thirty two bit width and adds the shared marker when the private indicator FUTEX_PRIVATE_FLAG is absent and propagates realtime clock indicator FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME with robust unlock indicator FUTEX_ROBUST_UNLOCK and robust list width indicator FUTEX_ROBUST_LIST32 when present in the operation.

Conversion from second-generation flags preserves the size selector and adds the shared marker when the private bit FUTEX2_PRIVATE is absent and propagates NUMA bit FUTEX2_NUMA with memory-policy bit FUTEX2_MPOL when present.

Flag validation rejects width FLAGS_SIZE_64 on non sixty four bit builds or compat tasks and currently accepts only width FLAGS_SIZE_32 and for requests with FLAGS_NUMA requires that the node identifier space plus the sentinel fits within the selected width. Value validation additionally rejects any input whose significant bits exceed the selected width.
Fault injection for futex paths is disabled in this configuration with the predicate unconditionally reporting no failure regardless of sharing mode.

Each hash bucket holds a waiter count in waiters plus a spin lock in lock protecting its chain plus a priority-sorted list in chain with cache-line alignment on symmetric multiprocessor builds to reduce contention.

Priority-inheritance state links owned instances for exit cleanup through list and embeds a proxy mutex through pi_mutex and records the current owner through owner and maintains a reference count through refcount and stores a lookup key through key for cleanup.
Callback type futex_wake_fn abstracts wake handling as receiving a wake queue head with the waiter object to wake allowing different wake strategies per waiter.

Waiter object futex_q carries priority linkage through list with blocked task through task and bucket synchronization through lock_ptr plus wake callback through wake with opaque data through wake_data plus lookup key through key with optional inheritance state through pi_state and real-time linkage through rt_waiter plus optional requeue key through requeue_pi_key with bitset selector through bitset and requeue state through requeue_state plus optional release reference through drop_fph with extra requeue wait state on fully preemptible builds.
Access direction for key handling uses a two-valued enumeration with FUTEX_READ distinguishing read from FUTEX_WRITE distinguishing write.
Bucket reference futex_bucket_ref bundles a global hash bucket through hb with an optional private hash context through fph allowing callers to track which table backs a lookup.
Private hash support is compiled out in this configuration where lookup futex_private_hash from an address space always yields null and release futex_private_hash_put is a no-op.
User word loads use a page-fault guard so faults on user addresses are contained and reported as faults rather than crashing with the caller mapping the outcome to EFAULT.
Enqueue futex_queue onto a bucket expects both the bucket lock with the waiter lock lock_ptr held on entry and releases both on exit after linking and assigning ownership.

Acquisition double_lock_hb of two bucket locks imposes a global order by bucket address swapping when needed so the lower address is always taken first with a nested annotation SINGLE_DEPTH_NESTING on the second acquisition when the buckets differ to inform lock validation.
Release double_unlock_hb of two bucket locks drops the first lock unconditionally and the second only when distinct mirroring the conditional second acquisition.
Vector wait record futex_vector pairs a user wait descriptor through w with its in-kernel waiter object through q in a single allocation.

Provides per-task preallocation ensuring a cached inheritance-state object exists leaving an occupied cache untouched and otherwise allocating and initializing empty linkage with null owner and single reference and empty key FUTEX_KEY_INIT reporting ENOMEM on failure where consumption clears the holder with an expectation that an object was present.

Reference acquisition get_pi_state on inheritance state requires a live object incrementing count refcount only when non-zero and warning otherwise so callers must hold a prior reference or otherwise guarantee liveness.

Attachment to existing inheritance state validates the user word against recorded ownership under serialization where stale reads yield EAGAIN and faults yield EFAULT and combinations of died bit FUTEX_OWNER_DIED with identifier mask FUTEX_TID_MASK distinguish empty versus populated owner with zero versus non-zero identifiers and missing owner without died indication with identifier mismatch yield EINVAL while success installs a new reference for the caller.

Attachment runs with the hash bucket lock already held and additionally serializes the user word plus state pair with the inheritance wait lock wait_lock held across re-read and checks and released on all paths.

Userspace may mix non-PI with PI uses or corrupt identifier and died bits so attachment treats null state with identifier mismatches and inconsistent died combinations as EINVAL rather than trusting the word.

Fresh inheritance state for a first waiter has post-conditions of proxy-locked ownership by the target with recorded lookup key for exit cleanup and linkage pi_state_list into the owner set and published owner with safety from bucket exclusion making publication safe without additional serialization and source object being the caller cache which becomes empty.

Provides initialization rt_mutex_init_proxy_locked of a proxy-owned mutex in locked state for inheritance use assigning a dedicated validation class pi_futex_key to its wait lock to avoid false recursion with hash-bucket locks on fully preemptible builds.
Base mutex post-conditions are an initialized wait lock wait_lock with an empty waiter tree RB_ROOT_CACHED and null owner performed under scoped initialization of the wait lock.

First-waiter attachment resolves the owner identifier to a task rejecting zero identifiers with EAGAIN and absent tasks through exit-race handling and refusing kernel threads PF_KTHREAD with EPERM and consulting task exit state under owner serialization where clean state FUTEX_STATE_OK proceeds to link new inheritance state and exiting state FUTEX_STATE_EXITING parks the waiter with EBUSY and dead or invalid states fall back to exit-race evaluation.

Private-key attachment borrows the waiter memory context mm without a reference so owner mismatch across address spaces yields EPERM and kernel-thread owners yield EPERM while identifier reuse versus exit races are disambiguated by re-reading the user word retrying with EAGAIN when changed and reporting ESRCH otherwise.

Owner lookup serializes against concurrent exit cleanup with the target owner lock pi_lock held across state inspection and linkage preserving the clean-state guarantee until the waiter is attached and dropping the lock before blocking on exit mutex exit_mutex when the owner is mid-cleanup.

User word updates for waiter bit FUTEX_WAITERS use guarded compare-exchange with fault-injection checks mapping access faults through and requesting EAGAIN when the observed word no longer matches the expected value.

Atomic lock attempt futex_lock_pi_atomic for inheritance futexes reports EFAULT on fault and rejects self-ownership masked by FUTEX_TID_MASK with EDEADLK and attaches to existing waiter state when present and takes over ownerless words while preserving died bit FUTEX_OWNER_DIED and optionally installing waiter state and otherwise sets waiter bit FUTEX_WAITERS before attaching as first waiter distinguishing takeover success with value one from attachment with value zero.

The atomic path treats a user word already owned by the caller as deadlock EDEADLK rather than blocking and treats concurrent user modification between read and update as retry EAGAIN preventing lost wakeups and self-block.

Wakeup wake_futex_pi transfers ownership to the highest-priority waiter by replacing the user word with waiter bit FUTEX_WAITERS plus new owner identifier with no died bit because the waker was owner then updating the recorded owner and unlocking the proxy mutex through a wake queue where mismatched words from racing unlocks yield EAGAIN or EINVAL and faults yield EFAULT.
Ownership transfer requires the inheritance wait lock wait_lock held on entry and releases it on all paths deferring actual wakeups until after release through a queued post-unlock step.

Owner fixup after stealing preserves died bit FUTEX_OWNER_DIED while replacing the identifier in the user word before mutating in-memory ownership so faults leave the recorded state consistent for later validation with already-fixed races detected and treated as success.
